title: Google Cloud Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in Google Cloud Platform. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: Does cloud hosting force a login backend?
questions.explanation: Google Cloud provides hosted services for computing, storage and data work. Begin by matching a service to a small, clear need. The example is a static-file problem. Cloud hosting does not force the app to have a backend.

questions.question: Which identifier do many commands use?
questions.explanation: A Google Cloud project groups resources and settings. It has a project name, a project ID and a project number with different roles. The display name is for people; the ID is used by many tools and APIs. This is a fictional planning example.

questions.question: What contains zones?
questions.explanation: A region is a geographic area. A zone is a deployment area within a region. Some resources are zonal, regional or global. The correct location field depends on the resource. A VM and an object-storage bucket do not use location settings in exactly the same way.

questions.question: What does a role group?
questions.explanation: A principal is an identity asking for access. An IAM role groups permissions, and a policy binds a role to principals at a resource scope. The design gives a specific reader limited access. Choose the actual predefined role from the service guide.

questions.question: Who does a service account represent?
questions.explanation: A service account represents an application or workload. It is different from a person's user account. A separate identity makes the workload's access easier to limit and review.

questions.question: What identifies the logo inside the bucket?
questions.explanation: Cloud Storage keeps objects in buckets. An object name identifies the object within its bucket. The bucket groups objects. A slash in the object name is useful organisation, not a requirement for a real folder.

questions.question: What must be reviewed before lifecycle cleanup?
questions.explanation: Versioning and lifecycle rules can help retain or clean up object versions. They need a deliberate policy so useful data is not lost or kept forever. The policy balances recovery and storage use. Actual rule syntax depends on the service configuration.

questions.question: What is a Compute Engine instance?
questions.explanation: Compute Engine provides virtual machines. You choose a machine configuration, image and location and manage the guest software. The VM is a rented computer, not a zero-maintenance static-file bucket.

questions.question: Which resource is regional here?
questions.explanation: Google Cloud VPC networks are global resources. Their subnets are regional. This is a useful distinction from some other cloud network models. The network can contain regional subnets. A subnet's addresses and region matter when attaching resources.

questions.question: What should an allow rule include?
questions.explanation: VPC firewall rules allow or deny selected traffic for targeted resources. A good rule names the needed sources, protocol and ports. The rule describes a narrow purpose. It should not open every port just because the machine is a test machine.

questions.question: Which service records event details?
questions.explanation: Cloud Logging records supported events. Cloud Monitoring tracks metrics and alert conditions. Use both to understand a problem. The metric shows a pattern; the log explains one event.

questions.question: Does a budget alert guarantee a spending stop?
questions.explanation: Budgets help monitor spend and send notifications. Labels help group costs by project purpose. Neither is a reason to skip cost review. The label helps organise the resources; the alert threshold is 3 units. These are invented numbers.
